desk.headline: Revenue up 5.3% to R$7.07bn, slight beat; profit down 18%; 2026 guidance reaffirmed on the call
results: Net revenue rose 5.3% to R$7.07bn, just above the analyst estimate; the year-ago figure is for TIM alone, before it bought V8.Tech and I-Systems.
Net profit fell 18% to R$990.7m (R$0.41 per share from R$0.50), as tax, financing and other costs rose.
Other operating expenses jumped to R$263m from R$65m; the nine-month accounts include a R$263m fair-value loss on an investment.
Nine-month operating cash flow rose to R$9.52bn; TIM paid R$2.03bn in dividends and bought back R$252m of shares.
TIM now fully owns fibre network firm I-Systems (completed May) and tech consultancy V8.Tech (January).

guidance.summary: The filing holds no outlook section. On the call, management said TIM is on track to meet its 2026 guidance, including shareholder payouts, but gave no new figures for 2027–2028.

points: Management said normalized EBITDA grew nearly 7% with a margin above 52%, helped by higher mobile revenue per user.
Competition in contract mobile was described as steady after a tougher Q2; TIM is holding prices to win more customers.
Fibre (Ultrafibra) revenue grew 12.7%, and business-customer revenue rose 19.3% over 12 months.
Lower interest-on-equity payouts raised the tax bill and slowed free cash flow growth; leverage is seen as comfortable.
The new controlling shareholder of Telecom Italia, Poste Italiane, has not changed priorities such as dividends, management said.
call.source: Quarterly financial statements (6-K) and call coverage: Investing.com transcript, 10 Nov 2026; Teletime, 9 Nov 2026

watch: Whether profit recovers as tax and financing costs settle.
Customer reaction to planned 2027 price increases on existing plans.
Delivery on 2026 shareholder payouts and any satellite partnership news by year end.
